title: Review: hams, jahr, shiddah and rakhawah: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed

source: Written for quran/y6 lesson 21 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Review rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 21. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

head: Shiddah (sound stops)
Rakhawah (sound flows)
rows: أ ج د ق ط ب ك ت
except tawassut: ل ن ع م ر

head: Not this
This
rows: A small, natural breath on ك and ت with a sukoon only

keywords.def: a quality of how a letter is said

questions.q: Describe the qualities of ق in «يَقُومُ» (83:6): jahr or hams? shiddah or rakhawah? heavy or light?
questions.a: Jahr, shiddah, isti'la (heavy), infitah; and qalqalah when it has a sukoon.

questions.q: Sifat cards (pupil PDF): for ص, ت, ع, ب write two qualities each. Today's rota group recites 83:7 to 12.
questions.a: ص: hams, rakhawah, isti'la, itbaq; ت: hams, shiddah, light; ع: jahr, tawassut; ب: jahr, shiddah, qalqalah.

questions.q: Extend: write the memory phrase for hams letters in Arabic.
Stretch: why do ك and ت have both shiddah and hams?
questions.a: The sound stops (shiddah) but a little breath is released after (hams).

questions.q: Which letter is jahr AND shiddah?
questions.a: A) د. د stops the breath (jahr) and stops the sound (shiddah). س and ه are hams and rakhawah.

questions.q: Think again: Hold your hand in front of your mouth and say 'tt' then 'dd'. What does your hand feel?
questions.a: On ت a little breath comes out (hams); on د the breath stops and the voice is strong (jahr).
